2026-09-11T12:39:28.7957088Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7957788Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7958359Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7959236Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7960132Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7961054Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7963886Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7967131Z >
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7971652Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7976851Z >
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7978324Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7980497Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7980817Z ### How to Use
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7981243Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7982427Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7983864Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7984174Z ```bash
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7989650Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7992019Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7994210Z ```
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7994620Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7995089Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-11T12:39:28.7998416Z ```bash
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8001012Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8002504Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8004820Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8006254Z ```
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8006631Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8007749Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8010185Z ```bash
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8011241Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8012491Z ```
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8012849Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8013405Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8014702Z ```bash
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8023019Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8025765Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8027082Z ```
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8028271Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8028769Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8029570Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8032444Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8036214Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8036519Z ```bash
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8037333Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8038879Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8041854Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8042465Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8043315Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8045170Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8046673Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8076551Z ```
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8077030Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8078497Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8080409Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8080722Z ```bash
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8082061Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8083659Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8084955Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8085746Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8086486Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8087961Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8088953Z ```
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8089326Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8089874Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8091305Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8093090Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8094869Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8096756Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8099402Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8100571Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8100964Z ### Notes
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8101349Z 
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8103106Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8105913Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8108249Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8110741Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8112976Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8114974Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8116749Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-11T12:39:28.8117995Z </mcp-clis>
